subject: Pioneer demo — model shortlist and ops tradeoffs
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@pioneer.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@pioneer.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pioneer demo — quick post-call recap + model shortlist

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo time today. Recap and recommended next steps below so we can keep momentum into a short pilot: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- Production-grade chat assistants for customer support (90% short exchanges, some 1–3 turns with a few long context docs)
- Hard SLO: P95 latency < 500ms for interactive flows; background batches can be slower
- Tight cost sensitivity for 1M messages/month (target <$1.75 per 1k tokens overall)
- Data residency in US region and SOC2 evidence needed

Redwood's initial model shortlist and rationale (attached: pioneer-benchmarks-030428.csv, prompt-sets-pioneer_v1.txt):
1) Redwood-Atlas-8B-q4 (recommended pilot default) — profile: 8B quantized, q4 float-matrix.
   - Why: best balance of 1) sub-350ms P50 interactive latency on c5g/g5-like infra, 2) competitive QoQ accuracy on our support intent/slot tests, 3) lowest incremental token cost in dedicated pools.
   - Tradeoffs: slightly higher failure modes on long multi-document retrieval prompts (we saw ~3% hallucination vs 13B variants).
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B-v2 — profile: strong instruction-following, very low cost.
   - Why: excellent throughput for high-concurrency chat and great on short-answer QA; P95 often under 420ms with batching.
   - Tradeoffs: slightly lower recall on multi-step extraction compared to 13B. Good fallback for low-cost paths.
3) Llama-2-13B-chat (rio-optimized) — profile: higher-quality long-context responses.
   - Why: highest quality on the prompt regression set (especially multi-step reasoning), lower error rate on compliance-sensitive phrasing.
   - Tradeoffs: ~1.8x cost vs Atlas-8B and P95 can approach 600–700ms unless pinned to dedicated capacity.

Benchmarks included (CSV): per-model P50/P95 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens estimated for hosted vs dedicated, and regression deltas vs our QA prompt set. See the attached file for raw numbers and the prompt pack for the evaluation prompts we ran.

Operational notes & flags:
- We recommend starting with Redwood Dedicated (small reserved pool) for the pilot to guarantee latency SLOs for the 13B option and to simplify fallbacks to Atlas-8B.
- We will enable prefix caching for common support prompts (expected ~20–30% token savings).
- Quality monitoring: we'll attach a small prompt-based regression guardrail (we referenced the prompt-sets-pioneer_v1.txt). If model regression crosses threshold X, automatic fallback to Atlas-8B is triggered.

Proposed immediate next steps (owner, ETA):
- Share benchmark CSV + prompt pack (Redwood) — done (attached).
- Confirm pilot scope (# users, sample data, success metrics) (Pioneer: Priya) — by 2028-04-06
- Sign pilot MOU for Dedicated pool (commercial) (Redwood sales: Ben) — draft by 2028-04-07
- Kickoff pilot config + access (Redwood infra: Marissa) — target 2028-04-14

If this aligns, I’ll circulate a short MOU and a one-week technical readiness checklist.

Thanks,
--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Attachments: pioneer-benchmarks-030428.csv (CSV, 45KB), prompt-sets-pioneer_v1.txt (TXT, 12KB)

From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@pioneer.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@pioneer.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Apr 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pioneer demo — quick post-call recap + model shortlist

Thanks Stephanie — very helpful write-up and clean shortlist. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- For the pilot scope: we can commit 1,000 daily conversation starts (roughly 30k/month) and will provide a 10k message sample dataset for initial evals.
- SOC2 + data residency are hard requirements; can you confirm the Dedicated path covers both?
- Regarding fallback: curious how hard it is to switch from Llama-2-13B-chat to Atlas-8B mid-session. Is there session-level consistency concerns?

Next steps from Pioneer:
- Priya will drop the sample dataset and a short success metric doc today.
- We can review the MOU draft early next week.

Quick note on timeline preference: we want the pilot running by 2028-04-18 if feasible.

On the session consistency question, I copied in Marissa — happy to take a short technical call if you think it's needed.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Soto
VP Product, Pioneer AI
alex.soto@pioneer.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Apr 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pioneer demo — quick post-call recap + model shortlist

Nice recap. A couple of operational clarifications I’ll handle: 

- Cost modeling: I ran a quick estimate using their 1k/day baseline scaled to 1M/mo (to stress test). Atlas-8B-q4 projected $0.95 per 1k tokens on dedicated; Llama-2-13B-chat ~ $1.75 per 1k tokens; Mistral-Instruct-7B-v2 ~ $0.65 per 1k tokens. I included this in the CSV.
- Fallback/session note (Alex question): switching models mid-conversation does risk small context drift if we don’t preserve or translate KV caches. For short 1–3 turn flows it's typically negligible — we can implement an in-session sticky routing policy for a given user ID for the session duration (30 minutes) to maintain consistency.
- Quantization suggestion: for Atlas-8B run with q4 and KV compression enabled; for Llama-2-13B we should recommend INT8 quant pipeline for the Dedicated pool if Pioneer opts for higher quality and tolerates cost.

I’ll spin up a short pilot MOU draft and attach the pilot-config-draft.pdf for the legal/commercial details.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachments: pilot-config-draft.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@pioneer.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@pioneer.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Apr 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pioneer demo — next steps and pilot kickoff plan

Alex / Priya — great, thank you. Confirming plan and a couple of action items so nothing slips: 

1) Pioneer: drop sample dataset + success metrics doc (Priya) — ETA end of day today.
2) Redwood (Ben): pilot MOU draft (we discussed) — Ben will send by 2028-04-07.
3) Redwood (Marissa + infra): prepare Dedicated pool config (Atlas-8B primary, Llama-2-13B can be added as higher-quality tier) — target 2028-04-14.
4) Technical check: short 30-minute call to validate session routing and prefix caching (we'll schedule with Marissa) — proposed 2028-04-11.

Pilot acceptance criteria (proposal):
- P95 tail for interactive flows <= 500ms for Atlas-8B in Dedicated; if Pioneer enables Llama-2-13B as a tier, we’ll aim for P95 <= 700ms with clear traffic split rules.
- Quality baseline: pass the Pioneer QA prompt pack with regression delta <= 5% vs the baseline short-answer set.
- Cost: scoped pilot to show projected 1M/mo cost within 15% of the estimates in the CSV.

If you approve, Ben and I will turn the MOU into a redline-ready doc and share an onboarding checklist (keys, network allowlist, SOC2 link).

Thanks again — excited to move this forward.

Best,
Stephanie
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
